text-field.when: Use TextField for a single line of user-entered text, such as a course name, email address, search phrase or URL. Choose TextArea when the content needs multiple lines, and a selection control when users must choose from known records.
how: Provide a visible label, or aria-label when the design deliberately omits a visible label. Use description for guidance and the supported type, placeholder, autoComplete and inputMode props for the input's purpose.
Use value with onValueChange for a host-controlled draft, or defaultValue for an uncontrolled field. Keep that choice stable; the callback receives the text directly rather than a DOM event.
Supply name for native form data. Use required, length limits or pattern where appropriate, and invalid with errorMessage for host validation. The host owns submission and persistence.
Choose density locally. A native form reset restores uncontrolled defaults; reset controlled host state explicitly when your form's reset policy requires it.

In the native reset example, the browser restores the uncontrolled email default while the host onReset restores the controlled name and clears its submission result. Submit validates locally; persistence remains host-owned.

Use placeholder for an empty-field hint while keeping a visible label (or the documented accessible-name option for TextField). Placeholder content is replaced by entered or selected content. The examples show placeholder-only, logical start, logical end and both-icon layouts independently at compact and comfortable density.

Supply startIcon and endIcon as decorative nodes, preferably owned icons. They follow text direction, remain hidden from assistive technology and add no tab stops. Keep buttons and other interactive controls outside these slots. Select keeps its dropdown chevron; ComboBox keeps its separate options button. AsyncMultiSelect forwards the same slots and placeholder to its query TextField.

For grouped text inputs, compose native fieldset and legend with separately labeled TextField or TextArea controls. Use instance-specific IDs for shared guidance and pass aria-describedby to each field when that guidance must be announced on focus. Each field owns its validation error association; RadioGroup is for one mutually exclusive choice, not a general field group. The lower input base remains internal.

text-area.when: Use TextArea for descriptions, notes and other text that should span multiple lines. It retains the field contract of TextField while exposing rows to establish a useful initial editing area.
how: Provide a label and optional description, then set rows for the expected amount of content. Use placeholder for an example rather than as the only label.
Pair value with onValueChange for controlled content, or use defaultValue for an uncontrolled draft. The callback receives the complete string.

Use name, required and supported length constraints for native forms; expose host validation through invalid and errorMessage. Reset controlled state in the host while uncontrolled values follow native form reset.
Apply disabled or readOnly according to whether the field should be unavailable or inspectable, and compare compact and comfortable density within the surrounding form.

Use startIcon and endIcon for decorative content at the logical edges. These aria-hidden slots add no tab stops and must not contain interactive actions. The multiline input retains its own ref, rows, resizing and native form value.

select.when: Use Select when users must choose one option from a known list and do not need to type a search query. Use ComboBox for searchable lists or AsyncMultiSelect when the host supplies search results and users can choose several records.
how: Supply label and options with unique, stable string IDs. Labels describe records; disabled options remain unavailable without changing their identity.

Control the selected ID with value and onValueChange, using null to clear it, or initialize an uncontrolled selection with defaultValue. Keep the control mode stable and supply a placeholder for an empty selection.
Use name for native form serialization and required, invalid and errorMessage for validation. Native reset restores uncontrolled defaults; controlled hosts decide how to reset their selected ID.

Use description for instructions and disabled or readOnly for the appropriate interaction state. Density comes from the surrounding scope rather than a Select density prop. The trigger reserves the width of the longest option or placeholder, so changing selection does not resize it. Host CSS can constrain the field width; longer selected values then truncate with an ellipsis while the popup retains the complete labels. The popup fits option labels independently of the selected value, stays at least as wide as the trigger when space permits, and is capped by the viewport. Dropdown scrollbars are thin, with hover/focus visibility and native touch/forced-color behavior.

Use placeholder for an empty-field hint while keeping a visible label (or the documented accessible-name option for TextField). Placeholder content is replaced by entered or selected content. The examples show placeholder-only, logical start, logical end and both-icon layouts independently at compact and comfortable density.

Supply startIcon and endIcon as decorative nodes, preferably owned icons. They follow text direction, remain hidden from assistive technology and add no tab stops. Keep buttons and other interactive controls outside these slots. Select keeps its dropdown chevron; ComboBox keeps its separate options button. AsyncMultiSelect forwards the same slots and placeholder to its query TextField.

combo-box.when: Use ComboBox to choose one record from locally supplied options while typing to narrow the list. The public Autocomplete primitive is an alias of this same component; neither alias fetches records or turns arbitrary input text into a selected business value. The option popup can grow beyond the input width to fit labels, up to the viewport limit.
how: Supply label and options with unique string IDs and presentation labels. The component filters those options locally; the host owns any fetching and result freshness.
Pair value with onValueChange for a controlled selected ID, or use defaultValue for an uncontrolled selection. null clears selection; typing a query and selecting an option are different actions.
Provide name for native form data, placeholder and description for guidance, and required or invalid with errorMessage for validation. Keep controlled state resets in the host.

Use disabled or readOnly for interaction restrictions and inherit density from the scope. Import ComboBox from the experimental entry or Autocomplete from the public primitives entry using the same prop contract.

Use placeholder for an empty-field hint while keeping a visible label (or the documented accessible-name option for TextField). Placeholder content is replaced by entered or selected content. The examples show placeholder-only, logical start, logical end and both-icon layouts independently at compact and comfortable density.

Supply startIcon and endIcon as decorative nodes, preferably owned icons. They follow text direction, remain hidden from assistive technology and add no tab stops. Keep buttons and other interactive controls outside these slots. Select keeps its dropdown chevron; ComboBox keeps its separate options button. AsyncMultiSelect forwards the same slots and placeholder to its query TextField.

async-multi-select.when: Use AsyncMultiSelect when users choose multiple records from host-owned search results. It separates the current query and result list from selected records, so a selection can remain visible when the next search no longer includes it.
how: Control query with onQueryChange and supply options for that query, each with a stable unique ID. Fetching, cancellation and stale-response rejection belong to the host; the component does not call an endpoint.
Use value and onValueChange for selected option records, or defaultValue for an uncontrolled initial selection. Preserve those records independently of the current result list.
Set loading during a pending request and errorMessage on failure. Provide onRetry to let the host retry its search; use description to explain the search and selection task.
Use name to serialize selected IDs in native form data. Query and controlled selection reset policy remain host-owned; disabled or readOnly prevents selection changes.

The host-owned async search example cancels timers/requests on query changes and unmount, rejects stale responses, retains selected records outside results, and models a recoverable failure/retry without a network endpoint.

Use placeholder for an empty-field hint while keeping a visible label (or the documented accessible-name option for TextField). Placeholder content is replaced by entered or selected content. The examples show placeholder-only, logical start, logical end and both-icon layouts independently at compact and comfortable density.

Supply startIcon and endIcon as decorative nodes, preferably owned icons. They follow text direction, remain hidden from assistive technology and add no tab stops. Keep buttons and other interactive controls outside these slots. Select keeps its dropdown chevron; ComboBox keeps its separate options button. AsyncMultiSelect forwards the same slots and placeholder to its query TextField.

checkbox.when: Use Checkbox for an independent yes/no choice, an agreement, or an item in a set where several choices can be selected. Use mixed to present a partially selected aggregate; use RadioGroup when exactly one of several options should be chosen.
how: Provide label and optional description. Pair checked with onCheckedChange for controlled state, or use defaultChecked for an uncontrolled initial choice.
Set mixed when the host's aggregate selection is partial. The host calculates that state and decides which items a checkbox activation selects or clears.

Supply name and value for native form submission, using required for a required agreement and invalid with errorMessage for host validation. An unchecked checkbox does not contribute its value to ordinary native form data.
Use disabled or readOnly for interaction restrictions. Native reset restores uncontrolled defaults; reset controlled checked and aggregate state through the host.

switch.when: Use Switch for an on/off preference such as reminders or a feature setting. Its label describes the setting, while the checked state describes whether it is enabled; the host decides whether changes apply immediately or wait for a form submission.
how: Provide a descriptive label and optional description. Use checked with onCheckedChange for a controlled preference, or defaultChecked to initialize uncontrolled state.
Connect the callback to host state and persistence policy. A visual state change alone does not save an account setting or send a request.
Use name and value when the switch participates in native form data. Native reset restores uncontrolled defaults; controlled preferences require a host reset policy.
Use disabled for an unavailable setting or readOnly when its value should remain inspectable without changes. Inherit spacing and target size from the local density scope.

radio-group.when: Use RadioGroup when users should see a small set of mutually exclusive choices at once, such as a delivery method or course visibility. Select is usually a better fit when the option list is too long to display in full.
how: Provide a group label and options with stable value strings and labels. Mark individual options disabled when they cannot currently be selected.

Pair value with onValueChange for controlled selection, or use defaultValue for the initial uncontrolled choice. The callback supplies the chosen value; the host owns option changes and selection policy.
Choose horizontal or vertical orientation for the surrounding layout. Use description for group guidance and disabled or readOnly to restrict interaction.
Supply name for native form data and required, invalid and errorMessage for validation. Native reset follows uncontrolled defaults; reset controlled selection explicitly.

Required only constrains enabled native radio inputs. With zero options or all options disabled, the group contributes no successful form value and cannot block native submission. The host must represent loading/unavailable choices and prevent submission when an answer is mandatory. Once an enabled option exists, native required validation blocks submission until an enabled option is chosen. Reset restores the latest uncontrolled default after host cancellation is known; controlled values remain host-owned and reset does not request an edit.

toggle-button.when: Use ToggleButton for an action with a persistent pressed state, such as bold formatting or an enabled view tool. Use Checkbox or Switch when the interaction represents a named form field or a setting rather than a toolbar action.
how: Supply readable children or an accessible name for the action. Pair selected with onSelectedChange for controlled pressed state, or use defaultSelected for an uncontrolled initial state.
Use onSelectedChange to receive the next pressed state. If you also provide onPress for a host command, avoid toggling the same state again in that callback.

Choose density locally and use disabled when the command is unavailable. ToggleButton is an action button; serialize application values separately rather than treating it as a native named form field.

toggle-button-group.when: Use ToggleButtonGroup for related pressed actions, such as choosing a view or enabling several formatting tools. It supports single or multiple selection while keeping the selected action IDs in a host-owned array.
how: Provide label and options with unique stable IDs and labels, plus optional icons or disabled states. Set selectionMode to single or multiple according to the action relationship.
Pair selectedIds with onSelectionChange for controlled state, or use defaultSelectedIds for an initial uncontrolled selection. In single mode, keep the controlled array to at most one ID.

Buttons default to equal widths based on the widest option, including icons and disabled options. Set buttonWidth to content for individual content-sized buttons. Constrained horizontal groups keep equal columns and wrap labels as needed. Set allowEmpty to false when a selected action must remain, and choose horizontal or vertical orientation. Apply density locally and disabled to make the entire group unavailable.
Connect selection to host commands or presentation state. The group is not a native form field; the host supplies any needed form serialization and reset behavior.

tag-group.when: Use TagGroup to display a host-owned collection of labels, especially selected filters or topics that users can remove. It represents the selected items themselves; use AsyncMultiSelect when users also need to search for and add records.
how: Supply label and items with unique IDs and labels. Use item disabled or removeLabel for per-item behavior and host-translated removal names.
Provide onRemove to receive the IDs requested for removal, then filter those IDs out of your host-owned items. Omit the callback for a non-removable collection.
Choose neutral or primary tone and compact or comfortable density. Use emptyContent to explain what happens after the final item is removed, and disabled to restrict the collection.
Keep adding records, persistence and undo policy in the host; TagGroup does not fetch records or save the collection.

date-field.when: Use DateField for keyboard-editable segmented date or local datetime entry without a calendar popup. Use DatePicker when users should also browse a calendar. A local datetime is not an instant until the host resolves it in an explicit timezone.
how: Provide label and choose kind: date uses a complete YYYY-MM-DD string, while datetime uses YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss without an offset or timezone. Partial editing stays within the field until a complete value is available.

Pair value with onValueChange for controlled values, using null for an empty field, or initialize with defaultValue. Keep supplied values valid for the selected kind and use matching min and max limits.

Use name, required, invalid and errorMessage for native form and host validation needs. Use description for guidance, disabled or readOnly for interaction state, and hourCycle for datetime presentation.

For an instant, call dateTimeToInstant with a host-selected timezone and ambiguity policy; do not infer timezone from locale. Native reset restores uncontrolled defaults, while controlled values follow the host's reset policy.

For local datetime values, call dateTimeToInstant with an explicit host IANA timezone. Reject ambiguous and nonexistent clock-change times by default, or deliberately choose earlier/later. Civil date values do not acquire a timezone for display.

Set entryMode="text" for flexible date-only typing, or keep the default "segments" for keyboard-adjustable date segments. Text accepts YYYY-MM-DD, YYYYMMDD, year-first slash/dot dates, locale-ordered numeric dates with two- or four-digit years, and localized or English month names. Valid input normalizes on blur or Enter; impossible dates stay invalid. Ambiguous numeric order follows Provider locale; relative prose requires a valid host referenceDate. Public callbacks and native form values remain Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD.

Flexible text accepts two-digit years using a fixed century rule: 00–49 map to 2000–2049 and 50–99 to 1950–1999. For example 1/1/26 becomes January 1, 2026; 1/1/84 becomes January 1, 1984. Numeric month/day order still follows the locale. Use four digits for other centuries. Impossible dates and host bounds remain invalid.

For deterministic relative text, supply referenceDate as a Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD civil date. The host derives today in its chosen timezone and pins the anchor for the editing session, including SSR/hydration. Without a valid referenceDate, relative phrases are rejected while absolute dates still work. The English grammar supports today/tomorrow/yesterday, next/last weekday, next/last day/week/month/year, in N days/weeks/months/years, and N units ago. Weekday names accept the active locale or English. Next/last weekdays are strictly later/earlier, weeks are seven days, and month/year offsets clamp at month end. Unknown prose/business-day rules are rejected; resolved values are ordinary absolute dates checked against existing bounds.

Relative date phrases use one SGUI-owned Gregorian resolver with no third-party parsing or arithmetic dependency. Supply an explicit civil reference date. Single-date week offsets shift seven civil days; the full-period range helper also accepts an explicit week-start policy. Supported grammar stays bounded; business, fiscal and holiday rules belong to the host.

Flexible date text also accepts a week from today, two weeks from today, in a month and a week ago. Word quantities are a or zero through twelve; nonnegative numeric quantities also work. From now means the same explicit civil reference date as from today. Range endpoints accept the same grammar, for example today - a week from today. A lone offset identifies one date rather than a complete range.

Flexible date fields do not add automatic format or relative-date help text. Keep previews clean; supply description explicitly when host-specific guidance is useful. Validation errors remain visible and associated with the input.

Flexible text entry defers visible validation feedback until Enter, blur or a native form-validation attempt. Editing again clears that feedback. Validity callbacks and Apply/submission guards still track incomplete drafts immediately. Explicit host invalid remains authoritative; reset or changed host values clear local validation feedback.

Pasting into date-only text entry edits a draft; blur or Enter validates and normalizes it. Invalid or partial text stays visible and blocks native submission without replacing the accepted form value. Segmented date/datetime fields do not promise the flexible whole-value paste grammar. Use native form validation, not a change callback alone: complete segment edits outside min/max may still request a value while native validity blocks submission.

time-field.when: Use for a local clock time without a date or timezone. The default textbox supports shorthand typing and a dropdown with separate hour, minute and day-period choices.
how: Pass value and onValueChange together for controlled values, or use defaultValue. Public values remain HH:mm:ss or null. Text entry is the default; entryMode="segments" retains the older segmented interaction. The ref remains the outer div.

Text accepts a/p or AM/PM suffixes (8a, 8:30 pm), localized day periods/digits, and 24-hour times with optional seconds. Blur or Enter normalizes valid text. Bare hours use 24-hour meaning: 8 is 08:00 and 20 is 20:00. Invalid input stays visible and blocks native form validity; it never silently rolls over or replaces the accepted value.

Choose hourCycle 12 or 24, or inherit the locale clock convention. Open the clock button or use Alt+Down from the textbox. Choose hour, minute and AM/PM (12-hour mode); Apply commits, Cancel/Escape discard popup changes. Existing nonzero seconds stay visible and editable in the popup. Options remain stable rather than cascading; every minute is available.

Use canonical min/max for a same-day local clock interval. Reversed or malformed bounds are invalid. Out-of-bounds typed values and popup candidates cannot commit. Disabled and read-only states prevent changes. Native accepted reset restores defaults silently; a prevented reset preserves edits; controlled hosts retain authority.

onValidityChange reports text/segment completeness and bounds even when a partial edit emits no onValueChange. Native form names serialize only accepted HH:mm:ss values. Keep persistence, appointment availability, dates, timezones and daylight-saving policy in the host.

Field corners follow the active theme. Joined input and icon controls retain rounded outside corners and a straight inner divider, with padding that keeps text and icons clear of rounded ends. The Material demo uses the same rounded field shape across text, selection and date/time controls.

Flexible time text accepts compact HMM/HHMM: 1300 means 13:00 and 315p means 3:15 pm. The final two digits are minutes; without a/p, compact values use the 24-hour clock. The configured hour cycle controls display. Invalid hours/minutes are rejected without rollover.

minuteStep suggests popup minute increments from 1–60 while retaining an existing off-step minute. Typed values are not rounded. getTimeUnavailableReason rejects host-defined local clock values; the host may close over a selected date for appointment rules.

Flexible text entry defers visible validation feedback until Enter, blur or a native form-validation attempt. Editing again clears that feedback. Validity callbacks and Apply/submission guards still track incomplete drafts immediately. Explicit host invalid remains authoritative; reset or changed host values clear local validation feedback.

Plain-text paste uses the time textbox grammar, including a/p suffixes, compact clock text and optional seconds. Paste edits the draft; blur or Enter validates and normalizes it, while Enter prevents implicit submission. Invalid/partial text blocks native submit and preserves accepted HH:mm:ss form values. Segmented time entry does not promise whole-time paste support.

calendar.when: Use Calendar when date browsing should remain visible within the page or a custom composition. It selects one day or several independent days; use DateRangeSelector for an inclusive interval and DatePicker for a compact field with a calendar popup.
how: Provide label and Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD values. In single selection use a date or null; in multiple selection use an array of dates. Match value and onValueChange to the selected mode, or use defaultValue for uncontrolled initialization.
Choose one, two or three consecutive visible months and firstDayOfWeek. Treat focusedDate and onFocusedDateChange separately from selected values: moving focus is not the same as selecting a day.
Supply min, max and unavailable date/reason records from host metadata. The component does not fetch availability; disabled or readOnly restricts the entire calendar.

Use Provider locale for presentation without changing serialized civil dates. Calendar is not a named native form field, so the host supplies serialization, submission and reset policy when composing a form.

Calendar columns adapt to the available width using owned typography and target-size tokens. Narrow months show locale-native weekday initials while date buttons retain complete accessible dates. When enlarged touch targets cannot fit, the date grid scrolls horizontally beneath its fixed month heading; keyboard focus reveals the active date with an inset focus ring without widening the page.

Calendar grids reserve six week rows so month navigation keeps a stable height. Day numbers are centered inside selection targets. Months default to seven tightly packed day targets (24px compact pointer height, 36px comfortable pointer height, and at least 44px for touch). Month width has a 12rem minimum to keep the heading and navigation usable, without stretching across its host. Multiple months wrap when the host is narrow; minimum targets and enlarged text may require local horizontal scrolling.

The accessible label is always retained. showTitle defaults to false; enable it for a visible title. The month/year is left aligned in LTR (logical start), with previous/next text buttons grouped at logical end. Paged month changes slide horizontally; RTL reverses direction, and reduced-motion preferences remove sliding. Navigation preserves the live grid and focus; outgoing month images are inert and hidden from assistive technology.

Set navigation="month-year" to add localized month/year dropdowns while keeping arrows. visibleYears defaults to 120, is limited to 1–9999 choices, and is constrained by the calendar min/max. Navigation changes focus/view without committing selection. Use explicit host min/max for birthday policy; keep direct text entry available for known dates.

getDateUnavailableReason supplies recurring host availability rules; renderDayContent supplies decorative day annotations. DateRangeSelector adds endpoint-aware range validation, length constraints, active endpoint selection and move/resize gestures.

date-picker.when: Use DatePicker when users should be able to type a date freehand or choose it from a calendar popup. Flexible text is the default; segmented date entry is optional. The popup inherits the selected component theme scope.
how: Flexible date entry (entryMode="text") is the default. Users may type ISO, locale-ordered numeric dates or named months and normalize on blur/Enter, or choose from the calendar. Set entryMode="segments" explicitly for segmented date entry. The combined datetime field continues to use segments.

The editable date and calendar button share one bordered control row. The label sits above, and description or validation text stays below the complete group. Both entry modes retain separate keyboard targets and the named calendar action.

Provide label and YYYY-MM-DD value with onValueChange for controlled selection, using null to clear, or defaultValue for an uncontrolled initial date. Use defaultFocusedDate to give an empty calendar a useful starting month.
Supply min, max and unavailable date/reason records from the host. An unavailable current date is presented as invalid; the host remains responsible for its business availability policy.
Use description, required, invalid and errorMessage for form guidance and validation. name serializes the date in native form data; disabled or readOnly prevents calendar activation.
Native form reset restores uncontrolled defaults and closes the popup. Controlled reset belongs to the host; date-only values remain civil dates and do not imply a timezone.

Calendar columns adapt to the available width using owned typography and target-size tokens. Narrow months show locale-native weekday initials while date buttons retain complete accessible dates. When enlarged touch targets cannot fit, the date grid scrolls horizontally beneath its fixed month heading; keyboard focus reveals the active date with an inset focus ring without widening the page.

Set entryMode="text" for flexible date-only typing, or keep the default "segments" for keyboard-adjustable date segments. Text accepts YYYY-MM-DD, YYYYMMDD, year-first slash/dot dates, locale-ordered numeric dates with two- or four-digit years, and localized or English month names. Valid input normalizes on blur or Enter; impossible dates stay invalid. Ambiguous numeric order follows Provider locale; relative prose requires a valid host referenceDate. Public callbacks and native form values remain Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD.

Month width has a 12rem minimum to keep the heading and navigation usable, without stretching across its host. Multiple months wrap when the host is narrow; minimum targets and enlarged text may require local horizontal scrolling.

The dropdown retains its accessible label and hides its visible title by default. Set showTitle to true to display one title. The month/year is left aligned in LTR (logical start), with previous/next text buttons grouped at logical end. Paged month changes slide horizontally; RTL reverses direction, and reduced-motion preferences remove sliding. Navigation preserves the live grid and focus; outgoing month images are inert and hidden from assistive technology.

Set navigation="month-year" to add localized month/year dropdowns while keeping arrows. visibleYears defaults to 120, is limited to 1–9999 choices, and is constrained by the calendar min/max. Navigation changes focus/view without committing selection. Use explicit host min/max for birthday policy; keep direct text entry available for known dates.

Use kind="datetime" for a local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss value, with hourCycle 12 or 24. The popup combines the date calendar and a TimeField; Apply commits both and Cancel or Escape discards popup edits. Incomplete or out-of-bounds times cannot Apply. Datetime entry uses segments even when entryMode is text. Date-only selection still commits immediately. Provide complete datetime min/max and date-only unavailable dates; the host supplies timezone conversion and daylight-saving policy.

The datetime popup now uses the default TimeField textbox and optional clock dropdown. Type shorthand such as 8a or choose hour/minute/day period, then apply the complete date/time transaction. Invalid time drafts block the outer Apply. The outer combined datetime field remains segmented.

Flexible text accepts two-digit years using a fixed century rule: 00–49 map to 2000–2049 and 50–99 to 1950–1999. For example 1/1/26 becomes January 1, 2026; 1/1/84 becomes January 1, 1984. Numeric month/day order still follows the locale. Use four digits for other centuries. Impossible dates and host bounds remain invalid.

The host derives today in its chosen timezone and pins the anchor for the editing session, including SSR/hydration. Without a valid referenceDate, relative phrases are rejected while absolute dates still work. Weekday names accept the active locale or English. Next/last weekdays are strictly later/earlier, weeks are seven days, and month/year offsets clamp at month end. Unknown prose/business-day rules are rejected; resolved values are ordinary absolute dates checked against existing bounds.

Field corners follow the active theme. Joined input and icon controls retain rounded outside corners and a straight inner divider, with padding that keeps text and icons clear of rounded ends. The Material demo uses the same rounded field shape across text, selection and date/time controls.

Relative date phrases use one SGUI-owned Gregorian resolver with no third-party parsing or arithmetic dependency. Supply an explicit civil reference date. Single-date week offsets shift seven civil days; the full-period range helper also accepts an explicit week-start policy. Supported grammar stays bounded; business, fiscal and holiday rules belong to the host.

Flexible date text also accepts a week from today, two weeks from today, in a month and a week ago. Word quantities are a or zero through twelve; nonnegative numeric quantities also work. From now means the same explicit civil reference date as from today. Range endpoints accept the same grammar, for example today - a week from today. A lone offset identifies one date rather than a complete range.

presentation is popover, dialog, drawer or auto (drawer on narrow screens). getDateUnavailableReason and renderDayContent are forwarded to its calendar; the host still validates accepted date-only values against its business rules.

Flexible date fields do not add automatic format or relative-date help text. Keep previews clean; supply description explicitly when host-specific guidance is useful. Validation errors remain visible and associated with the input.

Flexible text entry defers visible validation feedback until Enter, blur or a native form-validation attempt. Editing again clears that feedback. Validity callbacks and Apply/submission guards still track incomplete drafts immediately. Explicit host invalid remains authoritative; reset or changed host values clear local validation feedback.

Flexible text paste follows typing: blur or Enter commits a valid candidate; Enter prevents implicit submit. Inclusive min/max and host availability validate candidates. Required empty or invalid drafts block native submission while named fields retain the accepted value. FormData alone is not validation. Segmented/combined datetime whole-value paste is not a portable supported format; calendar and segment editing remain available.

date-range-picker.when: Use DateRangePicker for an inclusive date interval entered in one textbox or selected from a calendar dropdown. Relative complete periods use an explicit host reference date. DateRangeSelector keeps the calendars inline; DatePicker accepts one date.
how: Pair value with onValueChange for a controlled {start, end} range of YYYY-MM-DD strings, using null for no range, or initialize with defaultValue. Both endpoints are inclusive.
Supply host presets with stable IDs, labels, explicit ranges and optional descriptions. Use min, max and unavailable records for limits, plus months and firstDayOfWeek for calendar presentation.
Treat calendar edits as a draft until Apply commits through onValueChange. Cancel closes without committing; required prevents clearing, while disabled or readOnly prevents popup interaction.

Provide name to submit name.start and name.end in native form data. Native reset closes the popup and restores uncontrolled defaults; controlled host state, availability and persistence remain outside the component.

Calendar columns adapt to the available width using owned typography and target-size tokens. Narrow months show locale-native weekday initials while date buttons retain complete accessible dates. When enlarged touch targets cannot fit, the date grid scrolls horizontally beneath its fixed month heading; keyboard focus reveals the active date with an inset focus ring without widening the page.

Set entryMode="text" for flexible date-only typing, or explicitly choose "segments" for keyboard-adjustable date segments. Text accepts YYYY-MM-DD, YYYYMMDD, year-first slash/dot dates, locale-ordered numeric dates with two- or four-digit years, and localized or English month names. Valid input normalizes on blur or Enter; impossible dates stay invalid. Ambiguous numeric order follows Provider locale; relative prose requires a valid host referenceDate. Public callbacks and native form values remain Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD.

Calendar grids reserve six week rows so month navigation keeps a stable height. Day numbers are centered inside selection targets. Months default to seven tightly packed day targets (24px compact pointer height, 36px comfortable pointer height, and at least 44px for touch). Month width has a 12rem minimum to keep the heading and navigation usable, without stretching across its host. Multiple months wrap when the host is narrow; minimum targets and enlarged text may require local horizontal scrolling.

The localized range field opens a popup with editable start/end fields above the calendars. Set months={1}, months={2} or months={3} for consecutive months that wrap on narrow hosts. Text edits and calendar selection share the same draft; invalid text blocks Apply, while Cancel discards changes.

Set presetPlacement="side" for a bordered preset panel before the calendars, or "end" after them (left/right in LTR, reversed in RTL). Panels retain document/keyboard order when they wrap above or below the calendars in narrow hosts. The explicit "above" placement remains available. Matching draft ranges have a pressed preset; selection edits the draft until Apply. Bounds, unavailable dates and disabled/readOnly states still gate choices.

The preset list is fully configurable. Mix fixed DateRangePreset values with getRelativeDateRange(referenceDate, {unit, offset, weekStartsOn}) results. The helper resolves complete inclusive Gregorian weeks/months/years, with offset 0 for this period, -1 for the previous period and Monday-start weeks by default. Hosts supply the reference civil date in their reporting timezone and refresh it when needed. Business weeks, holidays and fiscal periods remain host-defined; pass their resolved ISO endpoints as ordinary presets. No implicit browser clock or fixed set of labels is required.

Selected and previewed ranges form connected bands within each visible week. Rounded caps mark the range endpoints, week-row edges and visible month boundaries; a one-day range remains rounded on both sides. Individual day focus stays visible, including RTL and forced colors. Calendar single/multiple selection remains separate day boxes.

The dropdown flips above or shifts upward within the viewport before introducing vertical scrolling. It may overlap its trigger when neither side has enough room. Content scrolls only when the full dropdown cannot fit in the visible viewport.

The dropdown retains its accessible label and hides its visible title by default. Set showTitle to true to display one title. The month/year is left aligned in LTR (logical start), with previous/next text buttons grouped at logical end. Paged month changes slide horizontally; RTL reverses direction, and reduced-motion preferences remove sliding. Navigation preserves the live grid and focus; outgoing month images are inert and hidden from assistive technology.

Set navigation="month-year" to add localized month/year dropdowns while keeping arrows. visibleYears defaults to 120, is limited to 1–9999 choices, and is constrained by the calendar min/max. Navigation changes focus/view without committing selection. Use explicit host min/max for birthday policy; keep direct text entry available for known dates.

Flexible text accepts two-digit years using a fixed century rule: 00–49 map to 2000–2049 and 50–99 to 1950–1999. For example 1/1/26 becomes January 1, 2026; 1/1/84 becomes January 1, 1984. Numeric month/day order still follows the locale. Use four digits for other centuries. Impossible dates and host bounds remain invalid.

For deterministic relative text, supply referenceDate as a Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD civil date. The host derives today in its chosen timezone and pins the anchor for the editing session, including SSR/hydration. Without a valid referenceDate, relative phrases are rejected while absolute dates still work. The English grammar supports today/tomorrow/yesterday, next/last weekday, next/last day/week/month/year, in N days/weeks/months/years, and N units ago. Weekday names accept the active locale or English. Next/last weekdays are strictly later/earlier, weeks are seven days, and month/year offsets clamp at month end. Unknown prose/business-day rules are rejected; resolved values are ordinary absolute dates checked against existing bounds.

Field corners follow the active theme. Joined input and icon controls retain rounded outside corners and a straight inner divider, with padding that keeps text and icons clear of rounded ends. The Material demo uses the same rounded field shape across text, selection and date/time controls.

The main field defaults to an editable range textbox with a separate calendar button. Enter two dates separated by a spaced dash, en/em dash or the word to, for example 1/1/2026 - 1/3/26. Blur or Enter normalizes accepted dates; locale order, named months and the fixed two-digit-year rule match DateField. Invalid, reversed, bounded or unavailable ranges remain drafts and block native form submission; hidden start/end fields retain the last accepted range.

Supply referenceDate to enable this/last/next week, month and year in the range textbox. These mean complete inclusive calendar periods, not rolling durations. Weeks use firstDayOfWeek, defaulting to Monday for relative resolution. The host supplies and pins its civil today; the control never reads a clock. Changing the reference does not move an accepted range. Business/fiscal rules remain host-supplied presets.

Use fieldMode="button" for a selection-only trigger. entryMode controls the separate endpoint fields inside the dropdown. description, invalid, errorMessage and onValidityChange apply to the outer field; onValueChange receives accepted absolute ISO ranges or null when an optional field is cleared. Calendar Apply commits and Cancel/Escape retains the accepted range.

Relative date phrases use one SGUI-owned Gregorian resolver with no third-party parsing or arithmetic dependency. Supply an explicit civil reference date. Single-date week offsets shift seven civil days; the full-period range helper also accepts an explicit week-start policy. Supported grammar stays bounded; business, fiscal and holiday rules belong to the host.

Flexible date text also accepts a week from today, two weeks from today, in a month and a week ago. Word quantities are a or zero through twelve; nonnegative numeric quantities also work. From now means the same explicit civil reference date as from today. Range endpoints accept the same grammar, for example today - a week from today. A lone offset identifies one date rather than a complete range.

Presets default to presetPlacement="side": a sidebar beside the calendars, with start/end fields sharing a row when space permits. Above and end placements remain available. The layout wraps within its host: narrow screens place side presets above the calendars in a wrapping row, and month columns wrap without reducing day targets. Range text and keyboard preview descriptions remain accessible without adding duplicate visual summaries below the calendar.

The dropdown uses content-sized Popover sizing, expanding to the configured months and presets up to the viewport width. The trigger field keeps its compact intrinsic width. If the reflowed content can fit vertically, the overlay shifts into view; otherwise the overlay scrolls to keep all fields and actions reachable.

rangeClickBehavior defaults to "adjust-end" and affects calendar pointer/keyboard activation only. With day selection and no fixed length, creating a range takes two activations in either order: 5th then 1st produces inclusive 1st–5th. With a complete 7th–16th draft, "restart" makes any click a new anchor with the end empty; "adjust-end" changes 13th to 7th–13th and 20th to 7th–20th, while clicking 5th or the current start restarts there; "adjust-start" changes 5th to 5th–16th and 13th to 13th–16th, while clicking 20th or the current end restarts there. After a restart, the second activation again completes in either direction.

With rangeClickBehavior="adjust-boundaries", a complete range stays complete through calendar clicks: 7th–16th plus 5th becomes 5th–16th; plus 13th becomes 7th–13th; plus 20th becomes 7th–20th. Inside-range clicks adjust the end. Clicking the start makes a one-day range; clicking the end is unchanged. Clear can empty an optional draft, while required disables Clear. Typed endpoint edits can still be incomplete or invalid, and presets supply their explicit ranges. All policies retain bounds/unavailability validation and Apply/Cancel ownership; calendar edits remain drafts by default; commitBehavior="immediate" commits complete valid selections and updates submitted endpoints.

rangeClickBehavior now names calendar activation policy; adjust-boundaries replaces the pre-release preserve-range name. Choose active-endpoint to explicitly edit Start or End, controlled through activeEndpoint/onActiveEndpointChange or defaultActiveEndpoint. Endpoint field focus also changes intent. Crossing the opposite boundary restarts at the clicked date with an empty end; equality creates a one-day range.

rangeDragBehavior is none, move, resize or move-and-resize (default). Drag the first or last selected day itself to resize that endpoint; an interior day moves both endpoints. There are no separate handles. Shift-drag any selected day to move the whole range, including two-day ranges. A one-day range grows toward the dragged date. Fixed length makes endpoint drags translate the whole interval, including resize-only mode. With bounded min/max length, the opposite edge follows once a limit is reached, keeping the grabbed endpoint under the pointer. Shift+Left/Right translates; Alt+Left/Right changes the end and Alt+Shift changes the start; endpoint keyboard edits use the same fixed/bounded length rules. Escape cancels. Invalid gesture release retains the previous draft and announces why it could not be applied.

rangeLength is either {mode:"fixed",value,unit:"days"|"nights"} or {mode:"bounded",min,max,unit}. Days include both endpoints; nights count the endpoint gap. Fixed length makes the first click a complete interval, subsequent clicks relocate it and resizing is disabled. Typed endpoints and presets must satisfy the same rules.

getDateUnavailableReason(date,{range,endpoint}) returns a translated reason or undefined. Use endpoint for arrival/departure distinctions and the current draft for selection-aware rules. Full-range validation checks every day; interior dates have endpoint null. Keep callbacks pure; hosts fetch and cache data separately. renderDayContent adds decorative day annotations while complete date names and availability descriptions remain accessible.

calendarNavigation="independent" gives each displayed month its own navigation. Add calendarEndpoints={["start","end"]} to assign From/To intent in paged mode: the first calendar edits start and the second edits end, independently of rangeClickBehavior or activeEndpoint. Missing/null entries keep the shared click policy; linked and scrolling layouts ignore the mapping. Either endpoint can be picked first. Crossing the other endpoint clears only that opposite endpoint; equality selects one day. Availability checks use the assigned endpoint; onActiveEndpointChange reports activation intent. Fixed length and whole-period selection take precedence; incomplete drafts cannot Apply. Text fields, presets and dragging keep their existing behavior. calendarLayout="scroll" renders scrollMonths consecutive months (default 12, maximum 120) in a bounded month browser. Linked paged months remain the default.

commitBehavior="apply" keeps drafts local. immediate commits complete valid calendar/preset selections; invalid drafts never commit. onDraftChange reports the local range independently of persistence. DateRangePicker presentation supports popover, dialog, drawer and auto; automatic narrow-screen reflow keeps the same popup content mounted.

selectionUnit="week", "month", "quarter" or "year" resolves an entire Gregorian period from a calendar activation; day is the default. firstDayOfWeek defines weeks. Any rangeLength constraint still applies, so choose compatible options. PeriodPicker wraps whole-period selection with its own input and actions.

DateRangePicker hides repeated dropdown endpoint fields by default (showFields=false); opt in with showFields. Inline DateRangeSelector also hides endpoint fields by default; opt in with showFields. Endpoint fields default to flexible text and normalize supported formats on blur or Enter; entryMode="segments" is an explicit alternative. showActions remains true unless an enclosing composition owns commit controls. With immediate commits, Cancel discards unfinished edits rather than undoing accepted values.

presetGroups accepts host-defined {id,label,presets,children} categories. A category selector exposes nested paths while preserving each preset as a resolved absolute range. No browser clock or third-party relative parsing is introduced. getDateRangeLength(range, "days"|"nights") uses owned civil math and returns NaN for malformed/reversed ranges.

Presets use a single-select list of compact labels, with a checkmark and subtle selected background. Arrow keys navigate and Enter/Space selects a draft. Descriptions remain available to assistive technology without adding visible rows; availability, Apply, Cancel and immediate commit rules are unchanged.

Flexible text entry defers visible validation feedback until Enter, blur or a native form-validation attempt. Editing again clears that feedback. Validity callbacks and Apply/submission guards still track incomplete drafts immediately. Explicit host invalid remains authoritative; reset or changed host values clear local validation feedback.

For example, a 7th–9th range capped at three inclusive days becomes 10th–12th when its end is dragged to the 12th. At minimum length, dragging inward pushes the opposite edge too; endpoints do not invert. Date bounds and availability never silently relocate a rejected drop: the prior draft is kept. Dropping outside this selector also rolls back. Move-only treats endpoint days as whole-range drag targets; resize-only leaves interior drags unchanged.

A drop uses its release position and the latest availability/bounds, not a cached preview. Disabling or making the control read-only, changing drag/length configuration, resetting or replacing the host value cancels an active gesture. Cross-month drops focus the actual destination calendar. Dragging a boundary validates its real start/end role independently of the active click endpoint; interior dates retain interior availability rules.

A pasted text range needs two valid ordered endpoints separated by a spaced hyphen, en/em dash, or to. Relative expressions need referenceDate. Blur or Enter commits valid text; partial, reversed, unavailable or out-of-bounds drafts stay visible and block native submission. Enter does not submit. FormData keeps the accepted name.start/name.end values, and accepted reset silently restores uncontrolled defaults; prevented reset preserves drafts.

how: Provide label and value with onValueChange for a controlled {start, end} range of YYYY-MM-DD strings, using null for empty, or initialize with defaultValue. Host endpoint changes replace the current draft.
Supply presets with explicit inclusive values and optional descriptions, plus min, max and unavailable date/reason records from the host. Incomplete, reversed or unavailable drafts cannot Apply.

Use onCancel for the host's cancellation response. Cancel restores the committed draft; Clear edits the draft and is unavailable when required. Set months, firstDayOfWeek and defaultFocusedDate for the calendar context.

Use name to serialize committed name.start and name.end values, and keep controlled form reset, availability, timezone conversion and persistence in the host. Locale changes presentation rather than the civil YYYY-MM-DD values.

The German and Arabic civil-range examples use explicit translation adapters and Provider locale scopes. Both preserve the same ISO civil dates; timezone conversion belongs to separate host datetime policy.

Calendar columns adapt to the available width using owned typography and target-size tokens. Narrow months show locale-native weekday initials while date buttons retain complete accessible dates. When enlarged touch targets cannot fit, the date grid scrolls horizontally beneath its fixed month heading; keyboard focus reveals the active date with an inset focus ring without widening the page.

Set entryMode="text" for flexible date-only typing, or explicitly choose "segments" for keyboard-adjustable date segments. Text accepts YYYY-MM-DD, YYYYMMDD, year-first slash/dot dates, locale-ordered numeric dates with two- or four-digit years, and localized or English month names. Valid input normalizes on blur or Enter; impossible dates stay invalid. Ambiguous numeric order follows Provider locale; relative prose requires a valid host referenceDate. Public callbacks and native form values remain Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD.

Calendar grids reserve six week rows so month navigation keeps a stable height. Day numbers are centered inside selection targets. Month width has a 12rem minimum to keep the heading and navigation usable, without stretching across its host. Multiple months wrap when the host is narrow; minimum targets and enlarged text may require local horizontal scrolling.

Set presetPlacement="side" for a bordered preset panel before the calendars, or "end" after them (left/right in LTR, reversed in RTL). Matching draft ranges have a pressed preset; selection edits the draft until Apply. Bounds, unavailable dates and disabled/readOnly states still gate choices.

Hosts supply the reference civil date in their reporting timezone and refresh it when needed. Business weeks, holidays and fiscal periods remain host-defined; pass their resolved ISO endpoints as ordinary presets. No implicit browser clock or fixed set of labels is required.

search-field.when: Use SearchField for query entry with an optional results dropdown. It owns search controls and interactions; the host supplies data and routing. Choose ComboBox for a selected form option ID, and AsyncMultiSelect for multiple selected records.
how: Import SearchField from the root, primitives or experimental entry and load the stylesheet in an owned theme scope. Supply label or aria-label, placeholder and items with unique stable IDs, labels, optional descriptions, keywords and hrefs.

Use value/onValueChange for host-controlled queries or defaultValue for an uncontrolled field. Contains filtering searches labels and keywords locally. filter="none" accepts already-filtered results; the host owns fetching, cancellation and stale-response rejection. showResults=false supports a standalone search input when results appear elsewhere.

The component owns its leading search icon, optional trailing decorative icon, clear action, portaled nonmodal dropdown, count/empty/loading/error messages, retry and native keyboard navigation. Arrows move between input and results; Home/End move within results; Escape closes and restores input focus. Visible labels remain accessible names.

Result hrefs use the SGUI navigation adapter and preserve modified native clicks. onResultSelect reports ordinary link activation or an action result. onSearch handles Enter in the input when supplied. Hosts decide whether selection replaces or clears the query and own navigation/persistence.

Keep meaningful labels, resultsLabel and emptyMessage for the context; resultCountLabel can localize contextual counts. showClearButton defaults true. disabled/readOnly block editing and dropdown opening. Named input values and accepted native resets retain host control. Density and theme propagate to result portals.

period-picker.when: Use PeriodPicker to select an entire calendar week, month, quarter or year. Month/year navigation in Calendar instead navigates toward an individual date.
how: Import PeriodPicker, load styles.css and provide a Provider or ThemeScope. Choose unit and supply a civil referenceDate for deterministic initial navigation. The fallback view is January 2000, not an implicit today.
Pair value and onValueChange with an inclusive DateRange or null, or supply defaultValue. Weeks start Monday unless firstDayOfWeek is sun. Quarters use Gregorian calendar quarters, not fiscal rules.

Choose a year and month/quarter, or choose any date in a week. Apply resolves the whole period and validates every date against min/max, explicit unavailable dates and the host availability callback. Cancel discards; optional Clear commits null. Native reset restores uncontrolled defaults.

The host owns fiscal conventions, reference date, translation, availability and persistence. name submits name.start/name.end. Presentation supports anchored popup, dialog, drawer or automatic narrow drawer.

Native required/custom validity remains active while the popup is closed. Invalid submission focuses the real trigger and announces the error; accepted named values remain canonical and unchanged by popup drafts. Read-only and disabled states prevent editing.

date-time-range-picker.when: Use DateTimeRangePicker for a complete local datetime interval; use DateRangePicker for civil days without clock time.
how: Import DateTimeRangePicker, load styles.css and provide a Provider or ThemeScope. Pair value/onValueChange with {start,end} canonical local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss strings or initialize defaultValue.

Choose start/end dates through flexible text/calendar fields and times through text/dropdowns. minuteStep suggests 1–60-minute choices; it does not round typed values. hourCycle chooses 12/24-hour display. Both endpoints remain a local draft until Apply.

Invalid, reversed, incomplete or unavailable candidates cannot Apply. Clear is disabled when required; Cancel discards. Native reset restores uncontrolled defaults.
